statusDetail: Coverage complete. Requested host redirects through three aliases to https://blacktoonurl.net/.

page.notes: A single Korean destination-directory page. No local application routes, forms, overlays, media, or authenticated flows were found. The four outbound destination cards represent the whole template.

paths.description: Requested homepage through the full redirect chain to the sole static destination-directory template; tested desktop, mobile, dark, reduced-motion, forced-colors, keyboard focus, no-JS/crawler, performance, network, security, accessibility, and memory conditions.
Representative unknown route used to inspect HTTP/not-found recovery behavior.

findings.summary: Fixed palette does not respond to the user’s colour-scheme preference
findings.evidence: Dark and default screenshots are byte-identical (49,296 bytes in the capture output), and the rendered CSS contains no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rule. The page happens to use dark outer chrome, but does not adapt to the preference.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Cards rely on viewport-era layout rather than component-level responsiveness
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found Bootstrap viewport breakpoints but no container-type or @container rule; the repeated card component is constrained by an inline max-width.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the card list an inline-size containment context and adapt card typography/spacing with container queries, retaining a simple fallback.

findings.summary: Primary buttons have no visible keyboard focus indicator
findings.evidence: The active primary .btn has outline: none 0px and box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 in the focused-state probe. The element receives focus, but there is no visible focus treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible outline or ring with sufficient offset; do not remove the browser outline without a replacement.

findings.summary: Invalid paths silently present the normal success page
findings.evidence: A request and screenshot for /nonexistent-audit-test rendered the same landing page as /. Users receive no not-found state, explanation, or recovery cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 response and show a concise Korean not-found message with links back to the current-domain directory.

findings.summary: Mobile LCP is outside the good range for a tiny static page
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP/LCP at 3.5 s and performance 0.83; the CDP trace measured LCP 1.94 s, showing variability but confirming the redirect/load path can miss the 2.5 s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse the redirect chain, serve the canonical page directly, and trim non-critical third-party work from initial load.

findings.summary: Three document redirects delay the canonical page
findings.evidence: HAR recorded blacktoon413.com → blacktoon.me → blacktoon415.com → blacktoonurl.net before content, with each document hop taking roughly 355–448 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Redirect every retired hostname directly to the canonical URL in one hop and add a canonical link on the destination.

findings.summary: Third-party analytics and a full framework dominate a 348-character page
findings.evidence: HAR shows 166,675 bytes of Google Tag Manager JavaScript plus 24,208 bytes of Bootstrap CSS for a page with 45 DOM nodes and no application interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the full Bootstrap payload with the small authored rules needed here and load analytics only when justified and consented.

findings.summary: Card descriptions fail WCAG text contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe measured #7c8085 on #fff at 3.97:1 for all four card descriptions, below the required 4.5:1 for 16 px normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker text token that reaches at least 4.5:1 on white and verify all card states.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy skips from h1 to h3
findings.evidence: Lighthouse heading-order audit failed; DOM inspection shows one H1 followed directly by four H3 card headings.
findings.suggestedFix: Use h2 for each card heading under the page h1 and retain a logical landmark structure.

findings.summary: Repeated link text does not describe destinations
findings.evidence: All four primary destination links are labelled only “바로가기” (“Go”), so link lists and crawlers cannot distinguish the BlackToon, Twitter, Naver, and Kakao destinations by anchor text.
findings.suggestedFix: Include the destination in each accessible link name, for example “블랙툰 바로가기”.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are inconsistent
findings.evidence: The audited hostname redirects through three domains, the final document has no rel=canonical, and /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 403 while robots.txt otherwise allows generic crawlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical host, redirect each alias directly, publish rel=canonical, and serve a crawlable sitemap consistent with robots.txt.

findings.summary: The public link directory has no share-preview or structured metadata
findings.evidence: DOM probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks despite the page representing a named web site/directory.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter preview tags and minimal WebSite or Organization JSON-LD matching visible content.

findings.summary: The canonical response lacks baseline security headers
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. HTTPS is present and no cookies or client secrets were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, nosniff, a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy at the canonical origin and redirects.

findings.evidence: Header inspection found no HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options), Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP on the canonical response.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure HSTS, CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, a strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Analytics is loaded by default and dominates transferred bytes
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; HAR attributes 166,675 of 195,644 transferred bytes to GTM and records a page-view request without any visible consent or preference control.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove analytics if it is not essential, or defer privacy-minimised analytics until an appropriate consent choice and honour user privacy signals.

findings.summary: Korean content is declared as English
findings.evidence: The document declares html lang="en" while its title, heading, descriptions, and controls are predominantly Korean, causing incorrect pronunciation and language handling in assistive technology.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="ko" (and an appropriate dir, normally ltr); mark isolated English spans only where needed.

findings.summary: Unknown routes have no intentional HTTP failure state
findings.evidence: The representative unknown route renders the normal directory rather than a distinct 404/error state, so stale or mistyped links look successful and offer no recovery context.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an accurate HTTP status and an actionable error page with retry/home options.

findings.summary: Background analytics cost is disproportionate to the page
findings.evidence: For 348 characters of body text, analytics contributes 166,675 bytes and a background collection request; it provides no visible user-facing capability.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the tracker or defer and batch only the minimum analytics needed after an appropriate user choice.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes almost the entire transfer budget
findings.evidence: HAR reports 195,242 of 195,644 bytes as third-party relative to the requested origin, led by GTM; even accounting for the canonical redirect target, the analytics script is 85% of all transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a small third-party budget, eliminate the redirect chain, and remove or defer GTM so resource use is proportionate to this static directory.
